description: Redwood Inference is running a focused Customer Success & Support initiative to (1) refresh escalation paths and SLA expectations across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private tiers, and (2) execute a “known-issues sprint” to publish the highest-impact workarounds into the knowledge base (and link them consistently from Support workflows). The project is driven by Customer Support leadership (Dev Patel) and CS leadership (Jasmine Liu, Rachel Kim), with close partnership from SRE (Sean Gallagher/Rafael Mendes), Platform (Priya Natarajan/Ethan Park/Mina Haddad), and DevEx/Docs. Goals: reduce time-to-triage and time-to-mitigation for customer-impacting incidents, standardize severity/priority language between Support (Jira) and Engineering planning (Linear), align Support SLAs with Engineering SLOs and on-call practices, and decrease repeat tickets by making workarounds discoverable and copy/paste-ready. Scope includes: escalation matrix (who/when/how), severity rubric (P0–P4 + Sev mapping), tiered SLAs (first response/updates/escalation triggers), Slack bridge conventions and incident comms alignment, Jira field/automation guidelines (SLA timers, required fields, linking), and a curated set of known-issues articles (symptoms, impact, affected models/regions, workarounds, and “when to escalate”). Out of scope: broad product roadmap changes not tied to top escalations; long-form training programs beyond quick reference and templates. Timeline: a 2-week sprint (planning week + execution week) with a follow-up week for adoption/cleanup (automation tweaks, backlog triage, and post-sprint metrics review). Key deliverables are primarily Confluence references (published), Google Drive working drafts and spreadsheets, a Linear workstream with dependencies and engineering follow-ups, a batch of Jira support tickets representing real escalation cases, Slack coordination threads (support bridges, comms decisions), and a small set of GitHub PRs to update redwood-docs/SDK/docs tooling to reflect the new playbook and KB content. Constraints: customer-sensitive details must stay out of broadly visible docs; playbook must reflect real on-call rotations and avoid bypassing established incident processes; SLA language must be consistent with enterprise contracts and Support coverage windows; workarounds must be validated by SRE/Eng and clearly marked as temporary when applicable.

files.description: Published escalation directory: routing by product area (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), who to page, when to involve SRE vs Platform vs Runtime, and backup contacts; includes coverage hours and handoff rules.

Standard severity rubric mapping Support priority (P0–P4) to incident severity (Sev0–Sev3), with concrete examples (streaming disconnects, region degradation, auth outage) and escalation triggers (error rate, affected customers, revenue risk).

Tiered SLA table (self_serve/dedicated/private/enterprise): first response targets, update cadence, escalation thresholds, after-hours policy, and guidance for credits requests and contract exceptions.
How Support starts a Slack bridge: naming, required context, required participants, how to link Jira SUP tickets, when to move to #incidents, and who owns customer-facing updates.
Exec escalation rules: when to involve VP CS, VP Eng, and Sales leadership; escalation summary template; decision log expectations (credits, custom mitigations, status page).
Customer comms templates for initial acknowledgement, mitigation update, workaround guidance, and resolution follow-up; includes tone guidance and what not to promise.
Support intake checklist: required fields (region, model, SDK version, request IDs), how to request logs safely, quick diagnostic steps, and when to open a known-issue vs new investigation.
Jira usage guidelines for SUP tickets: priority/severity selection, SLA fields (first_response_due_at/sla_due_at), linking to Slack threads, and resolution notes standards.
Sprint plan: selection criteria for top issues, owners/reviewers, publication checklist, and target metrics (ticket deflection, reduced time-to-mitigation).
Curated index of known issues with tags (region/model/tier), last-updated dates, and clear ‘when to escalate’ guidance; intended as the landing page for Support and CS.

KB article: symptoms (stream reset, truncated stream), likely causes, recommended retry/backoff, client-side timeouts, and temporary mitigations (disable HTTP/2, adjust keepalive) with escalation criteria.
KB article: explains 429 vs quota enforcement, how to interpret rate-limit headers, common SDK misconfigurations, and Support steps to validate account limits/telemetry.
KB article: Dedicated tier autoscaling oscillation patterns, how to identify via dashboards, config knobs (min replicas, scale-down cooldown), and when to involve SRE/capacity.
KB article: Private installer upgrade failure modes, safe rollback steps, required artifacts to collect (installer logs, cluster events), and escalation path to Private Deployments/Platform.
KB article: audit log lag symptoms, expected delivery SLOs, temporary mitigations (batch export window, retry policy), and how Support confirms pipeline backlog.
Guidance aligning Support emails, Slack bridges, and status page updates: what qualifies for a status event, approval flow, and how to keep customer comms consistent.
Reference mapping Support SLAs (response/update cadence) to Engineering SLOs (availability/latency) and how paging thresholds should relate to customer impact.
Analysis doc summarizing top recurring Support themes (by ticket volume and severity), proposed doc/UX fixes, and the shortlist chosen for the known-issues sprint.
Working draft notes: open questions, proposed severity language, coverage gaps, and feedback captured from Support/SRE/Platform before Confluence publication.
Sheet-style table: candidate issues, ticket counts, affected tiers, workaround readiness, doc owner, reviewer, and publication status.
Rough drafts of multiple workaround articles with placeholders for screenshots/log snippets, review comments, and final publishing checklist.
